title: God Is the Fear Killer
summary: Remember what God has done. Our conquered fears become fuel for our future praise, and in Christ we are free to laugh, praise and hope.
exhortation: The Lord has done great things for you. Think back on all God has done in your life: how he has restored your fortunes, and how what used to fill you with dread has been stripped of its power. In its place you have confidence and hope.

I was reading a commentator on this psalm who said that saints often feed their hopes on the carcasses of their slain fears. Our conquered fears become fuel for all our future praises. How incredible is that?

So go back. Recall, recount and remember the power of God at work in your life. If you're in the middle of a trial that is bringing fear and dread, remember the enemies he has already slain, the fears that once dominated your life and now have no power. Our God is the fear killer. He makes a graveyard of the old enemies that used to rule us.

You are free from the bondage of sin. You're free from a life consumed with yourself. You're free from addictions, from groupthink and peer pressure, from the dread of the past. And you're also free to do something: look at the middle of this passage. Their mouths were filled with laughter and shouts of joy. You're free to laugh, free to praise, free to hope. In Christ our fears are conquered, and our mouths are opened to give him praise, glory and honor. So let's sing this morning as people redeemed by the blood of the Lamb and freed from the bondage of sin.
prayer: Lord, thank you for conquering every fear. If we think back and remember, we will see your faithfulness time after time. Help us remember, and find courage, hope and strength in your many victories, and no greater victory than the one over sin and death that you won on the cross when you shed your blood for us, Jesus.

Jesus paid it all. You have conquered our greatest enemies. May we remember, and live in the goodness of what you have purchased for us. May we live in our position as children of God, as sons and heirs. What a miracle, what kindness and what grace. Thank you, Lord.
